evidence: Cic. Inv. 2.160: intellegentia est, per quam animus ea perspicit quae sunt (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The power of seeing into a thing, and the understanding it gives (with the genitive of the thing understood).

evidence: Cic. Flac. 4 (Lewis & Short’s chapter): ingeniōrum acūmen
Cic. Tusc. 1.6 (Lewis & Short’s chapter): ubi est acūmen tuum?
terms.comment: Literally a point or a sting; of the mind, penetration, shrewdness.
Cicero’s word, used once, for the insight into truth that is the first part of wisdom; to have insight into a thing is perspicere.

sources: Lewis & Short: intellegentia · Lewis & Short: acumen · Lewis & Short: perspicientia
